newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka declines comment on Tamil rebel claim.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka declines comment on Tamil rebel claim.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Foreign Affairs Ministry said on Monday it had no immediate comment on a Tamil Tiger rebel claim that Colombo was behind the killing of two of the group's officials in Paris.
"We have no immediate comment to make on the Tigers' claim," a ministry spokesman told Reuters.
Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) said on Sunday two of its members were shot dead in Paris the previous night and blamed the killings on Tamils collaborating with the Colombo government.

A statement from the LTTE's International Secretariat in London condemned the killing of their treasurer Kandiah Perinpanathan, and Kandiah Gajendran, editor of the Tamil weekly newspaper Eela Murasu.
It said the killings were part of the Sri Lankan government's attempt to hit the rebels' finances, and appeared to blame Tamils cooperating with Colombo.

"This dastardly act is considered by our organisation as part of the Sri Lankan government's international conspiracy to destroy the legitimate struggle of the Tamil people for freedom and peace by curbing the financial assistance provided by Tamil people all over the world," it added.
Paris police have said the two Sri Lankan Tamils, both in their 30s, were shot dead by a gunman in the predominantly immigrant La Chapelle district of northern Paris.
The Tamil Tiger rebels are fighting the Sri Lankan government for an independent Tamil homeland in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
More than 50,000 people have died in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year, according to government figures.
